It includes skill instructions and auxiliary scripts, not the server handlers or deployed tool schemas.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The MCP is included in Supermetrics plans with Data API access; the product page says access is unlocked with any subscription. A 14-day free trial is offered without a credit card. Campaign management is described as early access and free with an existing subscription.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Subscription plans are fixed price. Exact plan prices were not established from the sourced pricing page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Supermetrics says plans are fixed price and charges are not based on data volume moved. Trial period: 14 days. Studio AI Credits are a separate metered allowance for Studio features; no MCP per-call charge was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: MCP use requires a Supermetrics subscription with API access. Campaign writes require per-account write access and may require configured human approval. The account owner who connected an ad account enables write access. Users need sufficient permissions at the ad platform as well.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization/team administrators; ad-platform permissions also apply.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The hosted implementation is closed. The changelog describes tool safety hints (read-only, destructive, open-world) aligned with operations; it does not establish all annotation values for every tool. 2. Campaign changes can require approval configured per account: no approval, approval before going live, budget changes plus going live, or all live changes. New campaigns are created paused. 3. OAuth scopes are listed above; product access is restricted to the user's authorized accounts/data sources. Campaign write access is separately enabled per account by the connection owner, and ad-platform roles still apply. DCR, CIMD, PKCE S256 and revocation endpoint are advertised; token lifetime and client allowlists were not found. 4. No read-only endpoint, toolset filter, or URL/header mode was found. Beta/early-access features and audience prompt availability have conditions. Global endpoint; no regional MCP endpoint found. 5. Docs describe per-user/session isolation and authorization boundaries; no MCP-specific PII masking was found. AI Terms place responsibility for personal-data exclusion in third-party AI use on the customer. 6. Query limits, truncation and API limits appear in the changelog (data_query max_rows; fresh queries can use quota). No general MCP rate limit or per-call price was found. 7. Changelog documents parameter validation, allowed values/bounds, account matching corrections, and tool errors; hosted handler behavior is not public. 8. Campaign changes are logged in Hub Campaign change history. General MCP-call logs, telemetry contents, opt-out, and retention were not found. 9. contact_supermetrics explicitly sends product feedback or support/sales enquiries; this is a vendor-contact mechanism. No separate rating/survey tool found. 10. Server-distributed skills and prompts shape agent workflows; recommendations in descriptions/docs are not evidence of server enforcement. 11. Business Context persists across sessions at team, data-source and account scopes; more specific context takes precedence. 12. One global hosted MCP endpoint with a flat named tool list, plus MCP skill discovery and a conditional prompt; no nested MCP servers documented. 13. No raw arbitrary API, SQL, or script-execution tool was found in the official tool names/descriptions.

E_aggregated.token_method: No hosted server code, complete tool definitions/input schemas, or initialize instructions were publicly available to serialize. The repository is a plugin and skills distribution repo, not the deployed server.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The user must complete OAuth/login flows and connect or reauthenticate data sources through the supplied login links. Account owners configure campaign write access and approval policy in the Hub; the agent cannot enable that access through the documented tool list. Subscription purchase/plan changes are handled through the Hub or support. OAuth scopes include account tags, custom fields, data blending, and DWH transfers, but the official MCP tool lists reviewed do not name corresponding actions; scopes alone do not establish that these operations are exposed through this endpoint.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor recommends reviewing campaign details before enabling them and reviewing AI-assisted actions and cost impact. It advises users to ask the AI to show its work and to check results against the source platform. These are user/client recommendations; the evidence does not establish that every recommendation is enforced by the server.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The product page says: “Each user authenticates individually via OAuth 2.0. Per-session isolation means every user sees only the accounts and data sources they're authorized to access in Supermetrics.” It also says: “We never use your customer data to train public models.” AI Terms say Supermetrics does not use Customer Data to train external/general-purpose models, while third-party AI providers may process data under their own terms. Campaign edits are logged in Campaign change history. AI Terms put responsibility for excluding personal data from third-party AI features on the customer.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor says the MCP returns live data from successful source-platform API calls and does not estimate, infer, or fabricate values. It says campaign changes are logged, new campaigns start paused, and campaign history can support reversing some changes; removed campaigns cannot be recovered.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The docs describe OAuth-based account isolation, campaign write settings, approval policies, paused campaign creation, and campaign history. These product controls are documented, but the hosted server code was unavailable for independent verification. AI data-training and third-party provider statements are contractual/product claims, not verified server-side enforcement. The vendor distinguishes its own model-training use from processing by external AI providers.

contradictions: Official inventories differ: the pinned README names 16 tools, while the setup documentation names 19. Their union yields 21 names. These pages may reflect different release snapshots or tool splits; the authenticated endpoint's live tool list could not be retrieved.

The setup documentation describes some combined functions (for example manage_user_and_team and manage_business_context), while the hosted changelog says mixed read/write tools were split into get_* and manage_* tools, with manage_* tools retaining backward-compatible read actions. The current README and docs do not present identical names.

Protected-resource metadata lists 13 scopes, while authorization-server metadata lists a broader set of 24. The server metadata includes account_tags, custom_fields, data_blending and dwh_transfers scopes without corresponding named actions in the official MCP inventories reviewed. Scope availability does not itself prove MCP tools expose those operations.

The vendor product page says MCP access is unlocked with any subscription; the setup documentation says a valid subscription with Supermetrics API access is required. The product page's FAQ specifies plans that include Data API access.
observations_for_research: Tool inventories and names can change between official docs and the current public repository; both sources point to the same hosted endpoint.
Campaign mutations combine per-account write enablement, configurable approval conditions, paused-by-default campaign creation, and an external campaign-change history.
The server advertises persistent business context with team, data-source, and account scopes, where the most specific scope takes precedence.
The product exposes skills through MCP discovery and a conditional prompt in addition to tools; the repository also distributes skills through client plugins.
OAuth scope lists are broader than the tools explicitly named in the official MCP lists, leaving an observable gap between delegated permissions and documented actions.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages, local repository, commit record, and OAuth metadata. The public repository is not the hosted implementation; the hosted endpoint requires authentication, so its live tool schemas and initialize instructions were unavailable. Tool parameters are marked NOT PUBLISHED where official materials did not give MCP input schemas. Third-party listings were used only to compare counts/names, not as action evidence. Searches included official docs, changelog, product/pricing pages, legal/AI terms, endpoint pages, and repository files. No unsupported third-party action was added.
